title: Restriction on Entry of Certain Nonimmigrant Workers
date_evidence: Publication Date: September 23, 2026 (Presidential Documents, Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 183)
key_claim: The renewed presidential proclamation restricts H-1B entry for petitions not accompanied by a $100,000 payment, effective 21 September 2026 and expiring 21 September 2027 absent further extension, and states that the largest IT staffing and outsourcing firms reduced combined H-1B registrations from 24,946 to 2,055, a 92 percent decrease, since the prior year's proclamation.

title: H-1B shock continues: $100,000 fee extended through September 2027

title: India tech sector crosses $300 billion, driven by AI and GCCs
date_evidence: Publication Date: March 30, 2026 (initial); updated September 16, 2026, citing NASSCOM's Quarterly Industry Review
key_claim: NASSCOM's Quarterly Industry Review puts India's technology sector on track for $315.4 billion in FY26 revenue (6.1% growth from $297 billion in FY25), with over 1,580 GCCs and a GCC market exceeding $46 billion, and names rising US H-1B visa costs alongside AI demand and GCC expansion as growth drivers.
frame_summary: This source argues, in the industry's own voice, that the US visa fee has become a tailwind for India's technology sector rather than a threat to it.
verbatim_quote: The US$100,000 fee on new H-1B visa petitions — effective from the 2026 application cycle — is reinforcing India's structural advantage as an offshore delivery base.
